content.text:
I can see the issue. The problem is in the `mustSegregate` function. It only checks the primary class (e.g., "5" from "5.1") against the SEGREGATION table, but the table contains entries with divisions (e.g., "5.1", "5.2"). This means hazard classes with divisions are never matched correctly.

The fix is to check both the full class and the primary class when looking up the SEGREGATION table:

input.command:
git add src/cargo/hazmat.ts && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix hazmat segregation check to handle classes with divisions

The mustSegregate function was only comparing primary classes (e.g., "5" 
from "5.1") against the segregation table, but the table contains full 
class entries with divisions (e.g., "5.1", "5.2"). This prevented proper 
segregation of hazard classes with divisions like oxidisers and organic 
peroxides from explosives.

Now the function checks both the full class and primary class during 
lookup, ensuring all hazmat combinations are properly validated.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
